transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because I keep checking the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes over and over. I need to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are still where I left them, even if I checked just a few minutes earlier. It takes up far too much of my day.
When you feel the need to check those folders, drawers, or boxes again, is it because an unwanted thought or image suddenly pops into your mind that something might be missing or wrong?

Yes. I’ll get this thought that maybe I threw away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. Even though I know I probably didn’t, it keeps bothering me, and I feel terribly careless unless I go check.
When you check those folders or boxes, does it briefly relieve the anxious feeling?
Yes, for a little while. Once I open them and see everything is there, I feel calmer—but then the worry comes back, and I end up checking the same folders or boxes again.
Do these repeated checking urges feel unwanted and intrusive to you?

Yes. I know it doesn’t make sense, but the thought keeps needling at me—that I may have thrown away my husband’s tax papers or put a recipe in the wrong box. I can’t seem to let it go without feeling I’ve been terribly careless.
When you check those folders or boxes, do you also feel a need for them to be arranged or placed in a way that feels exactly right?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that. I’m mainly checking to make sure nothing is missing or in the wrong place, not because it has to look arranged a certain way.
When the worry comes up, do you feel driven to physically check the folders, drawers, or boxes again?

Yes. I feel like I have to go back and open them again, even if I checked just a few minutes earlier. I spend far too much of the day checking the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes to make sure the papers and keepsakes are still where I left them.
Do you try to resist the urge to check the folders, drawers, or boxes?
I do try, but then I keep thinking I might have missed something. Before long I’m opening the same folders or drawers again, even if I only checked them a few minutes ago.
At the time you feel the urge to check, do you believe the papers or keepsakes really are missing or misplaced?

Not exactly—I know it probably isn’t true. But I keep thinking I may have thrown away my husband’s old tax papers, or put a family recipe in the wrong box. It nags at me until I feel terribly careless, and then I have to check.
Do you also find yourself worrying a lot about many other everyday things, not just the papers, recipes, and keepsakes?
I’m not sure I worry a lot about other everyday things in the same way. It’s mainly these papers and keepsakes that get stuck in my mind.
Do these repeated checking behaviors feel excessive or unreasonable to you?

Yes. I know I’ve just checked, and it seems unreasonable to go back again, but I still spend far too much of the day opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes to make sure everything is where I left it.
Do you ever feel a strong need to arrange those folders, drawers, or boxes until they feel exactly right?
No, I don’t think that’s really it. I check that they’re there and in the right place, but I don’t feel I have to arrange them in some particular way until it feels right.
